operation.query_signature: The predictor chooses $p_t\in[0,1]$ while the adversary simultaneously chooses $y_t\in\{0,1\}$. Both may use past predictions and outcomes, but the adversary choosing $y_t$ cannot see the current realized randomized prediction $p_t$. After both act, $p_t,y_t$ is revealed. No true conditional mean or privileged prediction interface is supplied. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.

comparators.definition: $$\operatorname{Cal}_T=\sum_{p\in\{p_1,\ldots,p_T\}}\left|\sum_{t:p_t=p}(y_t-p_t)\right|.$$ Sum only over distinct forecast probabilities actually used. This is neither per-round absolute error nor binned approximate calibration.

protocols.adversary_information: Follow the model and oracle timing. Current private random realizations are not visible to the environment.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Output a probability $p_t\in[0,1]$ each round. Evaluation uses the realized prediction and outcome trajectories; predictions cannot be rewritten after the game ends.
protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: The predictor chooses $p_t\in[0,1]$ while the adversary simultaneously chooses $y_t\in\{0,1\}$.
Both players may use past predictions and outcomes. When choosing $y_t$, the adversary cannot observe the current realized random prediction $p_t$.
The quantity $p_t,y_t$ is revealed after both parties act. No true conditional mean or other privileged prediction interface is supplied.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
